posts.author: alex
posts.title: Voice notes, finally searchable.
posts.summary: A small app that transcribes voice notes and makes them searchable by meaning. The recordings and processing stay on your laptop.
posts.detail:
Alex built this to find ideas recorded on walks without listening through every note. Search works even when the exact wording is forgotten.

Built over a weekend with Whisper and a small local embedding model.
posts.question: Can someone try it, or is it still a personal tool?

comments.author: sam
comments.text: The search-by-meaning part is exactly what I’ve been missing. Does it handle a mix of languages?

comments.author: alex
comments.text: Yes, I’ve been using it with English and Mandarin in the same note.

comments.author: maya
comments.text: Would love to try this when you share it.

posts.author: maya
posts.title: An assistant that stays in the margin.
posts.summary: Highlight a passage in an article and ask about it without leaving the page. The answer includes the lines it used, so you can check it as you read.
posts.domain: A browser companion for close reading
posts.detail:
Maya built Margin to help with dense articles without moving the conversation into another tab. Margin sits next to the text and keeps every answer tied to the passage you selected.

It’s a small browser extension, built around a very ordinary reading habit.

comments.author: julien
comments.text: Keeping the source lines visible is a nice touch.

comments.author: sam
comments.text: I can see myself using this for papers.

posts.author: julien
posts.title: Meeting notes in. A task list out.
posts.summary: A workflow that pulls decisions, owners and due dates out of meeting notes. Every task is yours to review before it goes into your task manager.
posts.detail:
Julien focused on making the review step quick. Each task sits beside the sentence it came from, and the user can change the owner or date before exporting.

It’s being used for Julien’s own meetings first.

comments.author: nina
comments.text: Which task manager are you exporting to?

posts.author: nina
posts.title: Colour palettes from a sentence.
posts.summary: Describe a mood and get a few palettes ready to use. Each comes with contrast checks and CSS variables you can copy into your project.
posts.domain: Small palettes, ready for the web
posts.detail:
Nina’s tool uses the prompt as a starting point, then applies a simple constraint: every palette has a text colour, surface colour and accent with contrast checked.

You can tweak the colours and copy the variables directly into a stylesheet.

comments.author: maya
comments.text: The CSS export makes this useful straight away.

comments.author: alex
comments.text: I’d use this for small prototypes.

posts.author: sam
posts.title: A map of the papers on your desk.
posts.summary: Drop in a folder of PDFs. This local app groups related papers, explains the connections and links every note back to a page in the original.
posts.domain: Find the connections in your reading
posts.detail:
Sam built this to find half-remembered papers. It presents small groups of related ideas with the page references that connect them.

The files and index stay local.
